name: Yam Beetle (Yam Tuber Flea Beetle)
description: Beetles that damage yam tubers by creating holes and tunnels. Both adult beetles (feeding on tubers) and larvae (feeding on organic matter in soil) cause damage. Infested tubers have reduced market value and storage quality.
symptoms: Circular holes or pits on tuber surface
Shallow or deep tunnels within tubers
Dark, decaying tissue around feeding sites
Secondary rot organisms entering through beetle damage
Adult beetles may be found in soil near tubers at harvest
treatments: Apply carbofuran or chlorpyrifos to soil at planting and during tuber initiation
Use neem cake as soil amendment to repel beetles
Handpick and destroy adult beetles when visible
Set light traps to catch nocturnal adult beetles
prevention: Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
Use yam mounds treated with organic repellents
Treat yam setts with wood ash or neem powder before planting
Avoid planting yam in fields with history of beetle infestation
Harvest promptly at maturity to reduce exposure
